summary: Keep command clients usable when config gains unknown keys while daemon parsing stays strict

replay.detail: No graph, projection, claim replay or startup readiness change.

schema.detail: No database or config-version change; the shared strict Config schema is retained.

rules.detail: No replicated rule, checkpoint, authority, lease or lifecycle change.

compatibility.detail: New command clients ignore unknown top-level and nested config keys with one per-process escaped key-name-only stderr warning, including completion, capped at 16 paths and160 characters per path with explicit truncation. Known typed fields and validation remain strict. Daemon/server/setup/policy and local-state fleet/uninstall/admission paths stay strict; doctor reports bounded names and strict mode fails on them. Old deployed strict clients are not repaired; restrictive new settings cannot rely on older lenient clients honoring them.

downtime.detail: The parser change adds no daemon restart, migration or recovery work.

manual.detail: After an install adds config keys, replace stale clients on session PATHs and coordinate restarting affected sessions so they use the installed build. Old deployed strict clients can fail for one more key-adding upgrade cycle; verify the session client and daemon source versions. No live session restart is performed by this change.

recovery.detail: No native mailbox recovery or production acceptance is qualified. Setup rejects unknown keys before rewriting; its existing raw-TOML merge is unchanged and is not a comment/order preservation promise. Old clients must be upgraded rather than dropping newer settings.
